stem.en: Salt dissolving in water takes in a little heat; the glass gets slightly cooler. It happens by itself anyway. Why?

text.en: The ions spreading through the water gain far more ways than the small heat cost takes away. Free energy falls.
Because water pulls the ions off.

feedback.en: The pulls are why the heat cost is small, but pulls alone would not make an uphill-in-heat change run. The gain in ways does.

text.en: It does not really happen by itself; stirring makes it happen.

feedback.en: Unstirred salt dissolves too, just slowly. Stirring changes how fast, not whether.

text.en: Salt dissolving gives out heat, not takes it in.

feedback.en: Measure it: the glass cools. This is one of the changes that runs on ways alone.

explanation.en: Look at both dials. Heat slightly against. Ways strongly for. Weighed at room temperature, ways win.
